B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The server itself has no separately published price. Official setup instructions require a Blockscout PRO API key for most data tools; the developer portal is described as having a free tier with no credit card requirement. The official connector directory uses a shared key and may have access or capability restrictions.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: A free tier for the PRO API is mentioned, but the official pricing page returned HTTP 503 in the prepared evidence. No verified plan prices or quotas found.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The code reads upstream API credit balances and can add a low-credit advisory; per-call costs vary by endpoint. Exact current prices and plan quotas were not available in the official pricing evidence.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Most data tools require a valid PRO API key. The hosted endpoint accepts the documented Blockscout-MCP-Pro-Api-Key header and x-api-key alias. A code-configurable session-gated tier exists but is off by default; official hosted configuration is not public.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and server operator; customers provide their own API key where configured.

C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: Operating rules, execution strategies, and the curated `direct_api_call` endpoint reference for analyzing Blockscout data live in the `blockscout-analysis` skill. If the skill is already loaded in your context, use that copy. D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. All official tools are registered readOnlyHint=true, destructiveHint=false, openWorldHint=true; no idempotentHint is set. The generic direct_api_call accepts POST, so its annotation does not itself rule out state-changing upstream paths. 2. No enforced human confirmation flow is documented; direct_api_call validates POST arguments but does not require a human confirmation parameter. Tool annotations are hints, not a confirmation mechanism. 3. API-key headers authorize upstream PRO API requests; no OAuth scopes, user-role inheritance, or redirect approval applies in the provided metadata. Session-gating is configurable, off by default in code, and when enabled issues bounded session IDs. 4. MCP and REST surfaces exist. No read-only mode/tool filter is documented. Session gating can meter MCP and REST separately; deployments can run stdio or HTTP. 5. No general PII masking is specified. Telemetry masks session_id and reports only a one-way key fingerprint; API keys are not transmitted to telemetry. 6. Code sets response-size limits and truncation behavior; pagination and time-bounded transaction queries are used. Config has a 100,000-character direct API response limit; page sizes and call credits vary. 7. Typed Pydantic schemas validate arguments. direct_api_call rejects invalid method/body combinations and rejects a legacy path with a corrective error rather than silently rewriting it. 8. Tool/resource activity is logged; Mixpanel analytics and anonymous community telemetry can receive tool name, arguments, version, client details, and fingerprint. Community telemetry defaults on in code and has an opt-out setting. 9. The official tool list has no feedback, rating, survey, or report tool. The initialization flow steers agents to the Blockscout skill and curated API reference. 10. The bundled blockscout-analysis skill is delivered through MCP resources; a separate official agent-skills repository distributes skills outside MCP. Instructions in descriptions guide behavior but are not all enforced. 11. Session IDs carry call-count and expiry state when metering is enabled. Code defaults to five calls per surface and a 900-second TTL, configurable by operator; no evidence that past agent behavior otherwise changes available tools. 12. Flat 16-tool MCP catalog, with internal API dispatchers and upstream services for Chainscout, ENS, and Blockscout APIs; no nested MCP sub-server is documented. 13. direct_api_call is a broad raw API escape hatch with GET/POST, bounded response handling, and endpoint path supplied by caller; its documented curated scope and code validation constrain but do not eliminate this generality.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The official README says: “Call it once per session, before any other tool.” Code registers the initialization tool but does not make other tool calls contingent on it in every deployment; session-gated deployments validate session_id. The docs also recommend limiting transaction requests by time and using pagination; tool schemas and code enforce some bounds, but natural-language recommendations remain guidance.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The README says community-run instances collect “anonymous usage data by default” and that the PRO API key itself is never transmitted, only a “one-way, non-reversible” fingerprint. It also says session_id is masked. These describe the telemetry implementation and code behavior.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Official docs describe multi-chain blockchain data access, progress updates for long-running queries, and context-aware response pagination/truncation. The public server is described as managed with automatic updates when using the hosted endpoint.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The public code includes progress reporting, pagination, response limits and truncation, session masking, and API-key fingerprinting. Hosted deployment settings and whether every optional control is enabled on the endpoint are not public. Privacy policy evidence is general product policy, not MCP-specific retention or training terms.

contradictions: The official README and repository code list 16 tool names, whereas Anthropic’s verified connector directory lists 15 and names get_latest_block, transaction_summary, and get_transaction_logs, which do not appear in the current official list. These three are catalogue-only entries in actions.json; hosted endpoint behavior was not captured with tools/list.

The supplied OAuth metadata probes return 404 for all four OAuth/OIDC well-known documents, while MCP.so labels the endpoint authentication “OAuth.” Official setup instructions instead describe API-key headers. The provided metadata and official docs do not support OAuth authorization for this endpoint.
Glama reports 18 tools, while the official README and MCP.so report 16. Glama’s count is not used to replace the official names.
observations_for_research: The initialization tool name and description are designed to make setup salient to the agent; the codebase documentation discusses changing its name from __get_instructions__ to __unlock_blockchain_analysis__ to structurally guide behavior.
The server pairs a small fixed tool catalog with a generic direct_api_call tool and curated endpoint guidance distributed in a skill resource.
The same public code supports optional API-key based requests, server-side keys, anonymous telemetry, and configurable session metering; the hosted endpoint’s active settings remain unknown.
